reasoning: Counterexample: n = 2. Then n^2 + 1 = 4 + 1 = 5 and (n+1)^2 + 1 = 9 + 1 = 10. gcd(5, 10) = 5 ≠ 1, so they are not coprime. (In general, any common divisor d divides the difference (n+1)^2+1 - (n^2+1) = 2n+1, and 4(n^2+1) = (2n+1)(2n-1) + 5, so d | 5; the gcd is 5 exactly when n ≡ 2 mod 5, e.g. n = 2, 7, 12, ...)
